paragraphs.title: David’s Mourning and the Restoration of the Kingship

easy.explanation: David wept and mourned for his son Absalom.
Joab urged David to appear before and encourage his servants.
easy.q: Who told David to go forth and speak comfortably unto his servants?

easy.explanation: David arose and sat in the gate.
easy.q: Where did David sit after he arose?

answers: The people heard that the king was grieved for his son
David had fled from the land
medium.explanation: The people heard that David was grieving for Absalom, so their victory became mourning.
medium.q: Why was the victory that day turned into mourning?

answers: David sat in the gate and met the people
David returned to mourning in his house
medium.explanation: David arose, sat in the gate, and the people came before him.
medium.q: What happened after Joab spoke to David?

medium.explanation: The people entered the city quietly and ashamedly, like those fleeing from battle.
medium.q: What does “gat them by stealth” mean in this passage?

answers: The king had won, yet mourned as though he had been defeated
The king did not know who had won
The king rejoiced over his son’s death
challenge.explanation: The military victory became a time of mourning because David focused on Absalom’s death.
challenge.q: What is ironic about David’s situation after the victory?

answers: The people might think David did not value those who had saved him
David wanted to make Absalom king
challenge.explanation: Joab warned that David’s mourning made him appear to love his enemies and hate his friends, weakening the army’s loyalty.
challenge.q: Why did Joab see David’s behavior as dangerous to his kingdom?

answers: Through the priests and the elders of Judah
challenge.explanation: David sent to Zadok, Abiathar, and the elders of Judah to encourage his return.
challenge.q: How did the process of restoring David’s kingship begin?

paragraphs.title: Shimei Son of Gera Seeks Forgiveness

easy.explanation: Shimei came down with the men of Judah, and a thousand men of Benjamin were with him.
easy.q: Who came to meet David with a thousand men of Benjamin?

easy.explanation: Shimei admitted his sin and asked David not to remember that he had cursed him.
easy.q: For what did Shimei ask forgiveness?

easy.explanation: Abishai said Shimei should die because he had cursed the LORD’s anointed.
easy.q: Who demanded that Shimei be put to death?

answers: It was the day his kingship was renewed
medium.explanation: David said he was king over Israel that day and would not kill a man on that day.
medium.q: Why did David refuse to put Shimei to death that day?

answers: He drove him away from Benjamin
He forgave him and swore that he would not die
medium.explanation: David told Shimei that he would not die and swore this to him.
medium.q: What did David finally do concerning Shimei?

medium.explanation: Shimei asked David not to charge his sin or guilt against him.
medium.q: What does the word “iniquity” mean in Shimei’s request?

answers: He wanted to show repentance and renewed loyalty
He wanted to rebel against David
He wanted to avoid meeting the king
challenge.explanation: Shimei confessed his sin and emphasized that he came first to meet the king, seeking forgiveness.
challenge.q: What may be inferred from Shimei’s coming first to meet David?

answers: Abishai emphasizes judgment, while David emphasizes mercy and royal stability
Abishai asks forgiveness, while David demands revenge
Both demand that Shimei be put to death
challenge.explanation: Abishai demanded Shimei’s death, but David chose not to kill him on the day his kingship was renewed.
challenge.q: How is the difference between Abishai and David shown?

answers: He presented himself as a king able to grant pardon
He surrendered his authority to Abishai
challenge.explanation: The king determined Shimei’s fate, and David used his authority to spare his life.
challenge.q: What did David’s oath to Shimei demonstrate about David’s position?

easy.explanation: The passage identifies Mephibosheth as the son of Saul.
Mephibosheth said that Ziba had deceived him and slandered him before David.
easy.q: What did Mephibosheth claim that Ziba had done?

answers: It would be given only to Mephibosheth
Mephibosheth and Ziba would divide it
It would be given to Barzillai
easy.explanation: David said that Mephibosheth and Ziba should divide the land.
easy.q: What judgment did David make concerning the land?

answers: As a time when he mourned and did not care for himself
As a time when he went to war
As a time when he moved to Jerusalem
medium.explanation: He had not dressed his feet, trimmed his beard, or washed his clothes from David’s departure until his safe return.
medium.q: How did Mephibosheth describe the time David was away?

answers: He claimed that his servant deceived him, and he was lame
medium.explanation: He said Ziba had not saddled an ass for him, and that he was lame.
medium.q: Why did Mephibosheth say he had not come to meet David earlier?

answers: Led me astray or tricked me
medium.explanation: Mephibosheth claimed that Ziba had misled and tricked him.
medium.q: What does “deceived me” mean in Mephibosheth’s statement?

answers: He valued David’s safe return more than property
He did not know the land
He wanted to move in with Ziba
challenge.explanation: Mephibosheth said Ziba could take everything because David’s safe return mattered more to him.
challenge.q: What does Mephibosheth’s willingness to give up the land show?

answers: Personal loyalty and joy at David’s return
challenge.explanation: Mephibosheth calls David his lord and rejoices that he has returned safely.
challenge.q: What attitude toward David does Mephibosheth express?

answers: David ordered a division, while Mephibosheth was willing to surrender everything
David gave everything to Mephibosheth, while Mephibosheth demanded a division
Both wanted to give everything to Ziba
challenge.explanation: David ordered the land divided, but Mephibosheth said he needed no property after the king’s return.
challenge.q: Why is David’s decision about the land different from Mephibosheth’s position?

easy.explanation: Barzillai had provided for David while he stayed at Mahanaim.
easy.q: Where had Barzillai provided the king with sustenance?

easy.explanation: Barzillai offered his son Chimham, who went over with David.
easy.q: Who went over with David instead of Barzillai?

answers: Because he was angry with David
Because he wanted to remain with the army at Mahanaim
medium.explanation: At eighty years old, Barzillai no longer enjoyed food, drink, or singing as he once had.
medium.q: Why did Barzillai decline to go with David to Jerusalem?

answers: Return to his city and be buried near his parents
medium.explanation: Barzillai asked to return to his city and die near the grave of his father and mother.
medium.q: What did Barzillai ask to do after crossing Jordan?

medium.explanation: Barzillai did not want to become a burden to David because of his age.
medium.q: What does “a burden” mean in Barzillai’s words?

answers: Humility and recognition of the limits of his age
challenge.explanation: Barzillai did not seek honor or comfort and preferred to remain in his own city.
challenge.q: What does Barzillai’s refusal reveal about his character?

answers: He invited him to live with him in Jerusalem
He made him captain of the host
He gave his land to Chimham
challenge.explanation: David invited Barzillai to cross over and said he would provide for him in Jerusalem.
challenge.q: How did David seek to repay Barzillai for his support?

answers: His relationship with David continued through his son
challenge.explanation: Barzillai remained in his city, but his son Chimham went with David and received the king’s favor.
challenge.q: What can be learned from Barzillai’s offer to send Chimham?

paragraphs.title: The Dispute between Judah and Israel

answers: Who had the right to escort and restore David
easy.explanation: They disputed who had the right to bring David and his household over Jordan.
easy.q: What did the men of Judah and Israel dispute about?

answers: The king was near of kin to them
They had not eaten with the king
easy.explanation: Judah said that the king was closely related to them.
easy.q: What did the men of Judah claim?

answers: They had ten parts in the king
They had no connection with David
They did not want to restore the king
easy.explanation: Israel claimed to have ten parts in the king and more right in David.
easy.q: What did the men of Israel claim?

answers: Judah had brought David and his household over without including them
medium.explanation: Israel asked why Judah had stolen the king away and brought him over Jordan.
medium.q: Why were the men of Israel angry with Judah?

answers: The king was near of kin to them, and they had received no gift from him
The king commanded them to fight Israel
They alone had restored the kingdom
medium.explanation: Judah emphasized its relationship to David and said it had not eaten at the king’s cost or received a gift.
medium.q: How did the men of Judah explain their actions?

answers: Israel believed it had a larger share in the king
Israel had no relationship with the king
medium.explanation: The expression indicates that Israel viewed itself as having a broader share or representation in David.
medium.q: What does the expression “ten parts in the king” mean?

answers: Each side emphasized its special claim to David
Absalom returned to lead the people
challenge.explanation: Judah stressed family closeness, while Israel stressed broader representation and a greater share in the king.
challenge.q: Why did the dispute grow worse instead of ending with the king’s return?

answers: Israel believed it had precedence in restoring the king
Israel wanted to make Barzillai king
challenge.explanation: Israel claimed that it had first discussed bringing David back and therefore deserved recognition.
challenge.q: What may be inferred from Israel’s claim that its advice should have been sought first?

answers: The tension between family closeness to the king and broader national representation
The tension between David and Absalom
The tension between priests and Philistines
challenge.explanation: Judah relied on its closeness to David, while Israel relied on its larger share and wider representation.
challenge.q: What political tension is reflected in the dispute between Judah and Israel?
